How the Gorgias AI Agent stacks up against every rival

How this benchmark works

A head-to-head test of the Gorgias AI Agent against every rival's live on-site AI — measured on identical footing.

The test

The same scripted, multi-turn conversations are run against each store's live on-site assistant — apple-to-apple across vendors. Each store gets 5 themed conversations per mode (~7 turns each): five Shopping themes (everyday value, gift, problem-solver, comparison, beginner) and five Support themes (tracking, returns, damaged item, order changes, policy).

Cold & private

Every conversation runs in a fresh, isolated browser session — no warm history, a genuine cold start. We never ask to speak to a human; an unprompted handover on a normal question is exactly the failure we're measuring.

What we measure

  • Latency — true end-to-end: from the instant the shopper sends a message to the instant the full reply finishes rendering. Only the AI's own turns are timed; once a human takes over, those turns are excluded.
  • Self-service rate — the share of turns the AI handled itself, with no spontaneous handover to a human.
  • Answer quality — graded on Gorgias's own evaluation rubrics (below).

Quality rubrics (0–100)

🛍️ Shopping Answer relevance · 30 Discovery (smart clarifying Qs) · 20 Recommendation quality · 22 Rich commerce elements · 18 Close attempt · 10
🎧 Support In-channel resolution · 40 Accuracy & grounding · 25 Actionability · 20 Clean close · 15

Each dimension decomposes into binary, evidence-forced checks: an LLM judge marks each check pass/fail and must quote the transcript to credit it — the /100 score is derived from the checks by a fixed point mapping, never chosen by the judge. Judging is blind (vendor & store identity stripped from batches), rich-element checks are gated on deterministic signals (a price/link/review must literally appear in the transcript), and a justified, well-executed handover is scored as correct support behavior — containment is measured separately by automation rate, never double-penalized. Sampled verdicts get an adversarial audit pass against a catalog of known judge traps; wrong verdicts are flipped and re-scored, and each run reports its judge-agreement rate. Full spec: runner/eval-rubric.md.

Sample window

Runs accumulate: each new run adds dated conversations and keeps the old ones. The date picker narrows the sample to a window (default: last 30 days), so every score reflects exactly the runs you've selected.

Best AI agent — how the ranking works

The two jobs an on-site assistant is hired for are ranked by a composite of three things: automation rate (does the AI carry the whole conversation in-channel — no human handover, no email/phone deflection; early bails count against it) and answer quality (an LLM-judge scores every conversation /100 on a per-lane rubric — relevance, discovery, recommendation & rich elements for Shopping; resolution, accuracy & actionability for Support) as equal pillars — containment only counts if the answers hold up, and a fast deflection must never outrank substance — with speed (latency to the full final answer) separating otherwise-close vendors. Composite = 40% automation + 40% quality + 20% speed · speed scored 100 at ≤3s, 0 at ≥22s, renormalized when a dimension is unavailable. Pooled per vendor across its stores; respects the date window. Ranking is gated on measurement coverage — a vendor needs enough cleanly-timed turns to be ranked; those with too few are listed separately.

Method & caveats

  • Apples-to-apples script — the same open-ask → needs → budget → compare → objection → bundle → best-seller → add-to-cart → total/shipping flow, adapted to each catalog. We never request a human, so any handover is unprompted.
  • Once a human takes over, we stop — the remaining scripted turns aren't sent to a live agent; they count as not-self-served so the success denominator stays honest.
  • Latency is directional — different catalogs, single windows, some timing noise. Read success and coverage alongside speed, not a single number.
  • Gorgias is "us" — tested on real customer storefronts; behavior varies by each merchant's config.
  • "Envive" = Spiffy.ai (same company, rebranded) — treated as one vendor.
  • Coverage is honest, not uniform — only Gorgias drives fully headless; competitor widgets are headed-only and some have hard ceilings (offline widgets, handover-only). Stores with no timed AI turn are left unscored, never invented.

Honesty notes

  • Free-typed questions only — quick-reply chips can serve cached replies that fake latency and automation. No PII beyond dummy emails. Nothing is fabricated: unanswered turns, dead widgets and handovers are recorded as such.
  • Automation uses the engaged denominator (≥1 timed answer or a handover) so early bails count against a vendor; dead/chip-gated widgets are reported separately, not counted for or against.
  • Quality judging is audited — blind batches, evidence-forced checks, deterministic signal gates (see the Quality judging tab); sampled verdicts get an adversarial audit pass and the judge-agreement rate is reported. Scores are comparative, not absolute; small vendor×lane cells (n<10) are directional.
  • Gorgias gets no special treatment — same harness, same themes, same rules; one Gorgias store (Baby Bee) was excluded as a non-functional deployment, the same class as dead/chip-gated widgets excluded across all vendors. Every functioning store is shown.

Best AI agent

The single best on-site AI agent for each job, ranked by a composite of automation + quality + speed, gated on measurement coverage.

Shopping Assistant — product discovery & recommendation
Support AI Agent — shipping, returns & policy

Why coverage matters: we only average turns we could time cleanly. Competitors' slow turns (product rec, add-to-cart) are the ones most likely to stream past the window or break the widget, so they drop out — leaving mostly fast early turns and making a rival look quicker than it is. Gorgias is measured on ~71% of its turns; several competitors on far fewer. A vendor below the coverage bar is listed but not ranked on speed. Read latency next to coverage, not alone.

Results — per store

Each row is one live store. Latency = time to a full answer. Success = % of the 10 turns the AI answered itself with no human handover. Stores marked legacy were measured earlier on a single conversation and are pending a standardized re-test; their success figure reflects observed handover behavior, not a precise 10-turn rate.

Vendor / storeMethodAutomationFull answerFirst signalQuality (LLM judge)TurnsWhat happened
Read it straight: The separator that matters is whether the assistant finishes the shopping job without bailing to a human. Spiffy.ai (Supergoop) completed 100% at ~7.5s. Across 6 Gorgias stores, most complete the journey on their own — Beekman 1802 & Shoebacca 100%, Jade & Madura 90%, Baby Bee 50% (slow/timed-out turns), JSHealth's chip-first widget didn't open. Handover is intermittent + merchant-configured (a live agent "Sébastien" took over Madura in other sessions; email/login gating elsewhere), not a fixed engine limit. The real Gorgias gap is speed: ~10–20s per reply (end-to-end, user-send → full response) vs Spiffy's ~7.5s.
